name: Winter 2026

reviewed.titleJP: デッドアカウント
reviewed.ratingText: Finish Ep, since I already did that
reviewed.review: I ended up watching the whole episode, not because it was particularly great or anything—it was just one of those things where it was there. I was kind of curious about the hook, and it came a little bit later, and by then I was already going, so I finished the episode. The actual show itself is fine. It's not great, and I'm probably not gonna keep watching. But it does come from an interesting premise: ghosts have always haunted places that people have strong attachments to—mirrors, rooms, bathrooms, and other places. That's shifted into the digital realm and is now focused on mobile phones. So it's kind of an interesting modern take on the ghost-haunting premise. The actual execution is just meh.

reviewed.titleJP: カヤちゃんはコワくない
reviewed.review: This show is mid. Its production values are not great. The story could go somewhere fun—I feel like it's kind of going for an Anya Forger kind of thing with the main character, but the rest of the show isn't at Spy x Family's level. It's basically just Anya at preschool. I have no interest in finding out if Kaya-chan is scary or not.

reviewed.titleEN: The Daily Life of a Part-time Torturer
reviewed.titleJP: 拷問バイトくんの日常
reviewed.ratingText: Maybe We Shouldn't Make Shows Literally Glorifying Torture
reviewed.review: This show features pretty boys and girls torturing people. The premise is that, apparently, torture is legal in this world, but it's very flimsily done. The starting premise is that the main character is supposedly so good at all of his previous part-time jobs that everyone wants him to take over their businesses, but he just doesn't want to do it—he gets bored with the previous 58 jobs he's had. However, he finds this job (literally torturing people) and he loves it! The main issue isn't just that he's mega-literally torturing people, it's that they don't actually show him doing the horrible things he's doing to people. If you saw him doing those things, you would immediately despise him. That doesn't work, because he's supposed to be a likable main character even though you see him sitting there—literally with people strapped down in chairs—then they cut away, the victims making ouchie sounds, and he's got pliers and other instruments of pain. It's awful. It's peak 2026+. Don't watch it.

reviewed.titleEN: A Misanthrope Teaches a Class for Demi-Humans
reviewed.titleJP: 人外教室の人間嫌い教師
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: Guy goes from hanging out and living off his mom for two years playing games to a job as a human male teacher at an all-female, cute demi-human girls' high school. It's everything that you think it is.

reviewed.titleJP: 花ざかりの君たちへ
reviewed.review: Beautiful boys' high school, with a girl pretending to be a boy at the school. Everything else follows from that. I am done now.

reviewed.titleEN: Oedo Fire Slayer -The Legend of Phoenix-
reviewed.titleJP: 火喰鳥 羽州ぼろ鳶組
reviewed.review: So it looks like it's gonna be some sort of sentai show about Tokugawa-era super firefighters who are also samurai. The character art is done with heavy 3D CG—it looks fine. Is this going to be a good show? I'm not interested enough to spend my time watching to find out.

reviewed.titleEN: Shiboyugi: Playing Death Games to Put Food on the Table
reviewed.titleJP: 死亡遊戯で飯を食う。
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: The first episode is ~50 minutes long, so I watched about 15 minutes of it. I still have no idea about the characters, plot, art style, production... really anything. It's supposed to be a death-game type of show, but it feels kind of like a weird version of Bakemonogatari in terms of some of the art style and overlays. But... it's not done as well, and I'm not interested in caring about whether these people will make it out alive or not. That sucks because I love me a good death game, and this one just isn't working for me. There's no death and there's no game.

reviewed.titleJP: アルネの事件簿
reviewed.review: Fine? I guess—I mean, it doesn't seem bad. It also doesn't have anything really making me say, "all right, this is totally worth my time to watch." It could be a show that gets good and interesting, but I've got my suspicions. It's gonna be stupid.

reviewed.titleJP: 多聞くん今どっち！？
reviewed.ratingText: Not My PET Bottle of Hojicha
reviewed.review: Face Off the group?! The show is fine. It's actually kind of fun as a thing where a 16-year-old girl meets her oshi—she gets a job as his house cleaner, and the dude is a total weirdo—but that's fine. I'm not going to keep watching it, but it seems OK. I have no idea how it will evolve. I assume it will, and I won't find out.

reviewed.titleEN: The Villainess Is Adored by the Prince of the Neighbor Kingdom
reviewed.titleJP: 悪役令嬢は隣国の王太子に溺愛される
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: Blah, lame. This is the worst version of several other shows I've done recently that are actually pretty good—the "excuse me, may I hit you one last time" shows, and the "oyaji gets transferred into the shoujo game" shows. Plus, from the opening, it appears this show also has 85 other things going on, so it feels like it's trying to do too much and nothing is interesting. Pass.

reviewed.titleJP: 違国日記
reviewed.review: Nice opening and first segment. I think it probably gives a good feeling for what the entire show is, in the feels and the vibes and everything there. Pretty good production values, nice look at kitchen food preparation type things. It's a show where you watch the first few minutes, and if you're not interested in the characters and where they're gonna go, then just immediately bail, 'cause I hope it's not gonna betray that anyway. It looks like it could be pretty good.

reviewed.titleEN: The Invisible Man and His Soon-to-Be Wife
reviewed.titleJP: 透明男と人間女～そのうち夫婦になるふたり～
reviewed.review: I wonder if the purpose of having the main character be invisible is just to have the person be literally the epitome of a non-character. It's fine, I guess—it's one of those kind of romantic shows. The only thing that's kind of interesting is that the world seems to be filled with a bunch of people who have different answers, with amorphous types and things, but I'm not interested enough to find out more.

reviewed.titleEN: Tune In to the Midnight Heart
reviewed.titleJP: 真夜中ハートチューン
reviewed.review: It's pretty boring. The main guy is very unlikable, and there are some cute girls, and it's high school, and blah blah blah. Skip. Next.

reviewed.titleJP: うるわしの宵の月
reviewed.review: The show is fine, potentially kind of cool. The main character is Utena-ish, but with less combat. There are two princes, so it's basically a Spin Doctors song.

reviewed.titleJP: ダーウィン事変
reviewed.review: Could it be interesting? It seems like it's gonna be a high school setting, coming-of-age story with animal rights and terrorist stuff. The character designs look very much like Urasawa's stuff; production seems fine. I'm probably not gonna watch it, if only because it's on Amazon, which for me means a pile of ads, and I don't tend to think about loading up Amazon—so it has to be exceptional for me to watch something on Amazon.

reviewed.titleJP: 藤本タツキ 17-26 [out of season review]
reviewed.review: I finally watched an episode of this, so this is an out-of-order review. S-tier. It's fabulous. At least episode one was incredible—so well done, one of those things where you watch it and you're like, "yeah, just make good anime and everything in the world will be better."

reviewed.titleEN: You don't know Gunma yet.: Reiwa version
reviewed.titleJP: お前はまだグンマを知らない～令和版～
reviewed.review: Well, this show was fabulous. It's a series of 12 three-minute episodes done as kind of a weird suspense-horror show, and then the ED is adorable, and then you learn something about different parts of Gunma: the food, the culture. This is definitely an A+ show. Would it be as highly rated if the episodes were longer? No way, but they knew exactly how long to make these episodes.

reviewed.titleJP: Fate/strange Fake
reviewed.review: So I haven't really watched any Fate stuff, maybe ever. It seems fine—it's A-1 Pictures and a good budget. Am I gonna watch more? Probably not, but mostly just because there's a lot of technobabble behind it, and it's hard to tell if I'm expected to know this, because I should've been watching Fate shows for the last 25 years.

reviewed.titleEN: You and I Are Polar Opposites
reviewed.titleJP: 正反対な君と僕
reviewed.review: Nice production values, a fun OP—it looks like it could be an interesting show. Is it probably gonna be some show that changes my life? No, but I often find I have a high-school-something show that I watch most seasons, and this one might be the one I watch this season. Solid first five minutes.

reviewed.titleJP: 勇者のクズ
reviewed.review: Kind of a fun show. I get some very '90s action vibes from it, like that "Blue Seed" kind of feeling. It's definitely a modern show, but I still get some of those feelings, so I've got hopes that it could be a fun action show.

reviewed.titleJP: シャンピニオンの魔女
reviewed.review: Actually, a fairly interesting beginning to the show. Cool musical intro—I liked the opening. I'm not quite sure how I feel about the animation style yet, but it seems to be reasonably well done. This show has potential to be interesting.

reviewed.titleJP: DARK MOON -黒の月: 月の祭壇-
reviewed.review: K-pop boys vampire reverse harem show. Seems fine for that, so if that's what you're into, go for it.

reviewed.titleEN: Isekai Office Worker: The Other World's Books Depend on the Bean Counter
reviewed.titleJP: 異世界の沙汰は社畜次第
reviewed.review: The show seems fine. The isekai was a magical being that dragged people into another dimension, and the main character was accidentally dragged in along with the chosen savior maiden. So at least it wasn't one of the dumb reincarnation or stat-screen things. Beyond that, I can't quite tell if it's going more for a shoujo audience or what, but it seems fine. It's not great. I probably won't watch it, but I've seen plenty of worse things this season.

reviewed.titleJP: エリスの聖杯
reviewed.review: Five minutes in, I'm still very unsure what type of show this is. I'll take that as a good sign. The production values seem pretty good. Voices, character designs, etc., are all fine. I can't tell if it's gonna go really shoujo style or if it's gonna be a little more interesting. But it's not a dungeon adventure, and it's not an isekai, so I'll take this as a positive sign.

reviewed.titleJP: 魔都精兵のスレイブ
reviewed.review: I don't think I really have anything much to say about this show. It's the same thing it was in the first one. I forgot that the key thing is that the main character is quite literally turned into a slave of the leading lady. It's miserable. The coolest thing was that the monsters kind of look like Sachiel from Evangelion, so that's a thing.

reviewed.titleJP: 穏やか貴族の休暇のすすめ
reviewed.review: OK, so the show is fine—it's a shoujo show. But I can't tell if the main character has been isekai'd or is just someone out of place. I guess that's a good thing: from the first five minutes, it's not 100% clear to me what will happen in the show. But I know there will definitely be ikemen.

reviewed.titleJP: 転生したらドラゴンの卵だった ～最強以外目指さねぇ～
reviewed.review: So the title did not lie about the content of the show. We got a status screen and a God-voice overlay about 20 seconds into the show. All the production values are terrible. The opening is just garbage—complete trash. I'd say the best thing about the opening is that it kind of looks like a Pokémon thing, but then the audience clearly isn't a kids'-show audience, going by the vocabulary and everything else they're doing, so it's awful.

reviewed.titleEN: Hell Mode: The Hardcore Gamer Dominates in Another World with Garbage Balancing
reviewed.titleJP: ヘルモード ～やり込み好きのゲーマーは廃設定の異世界で無双する～
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: Another show for which the question is "why?" Why anybody would spend any amount of time, effort, or energy making this thing is beyond me. I hope they got paid, at least—I don't even know what to say. It's dumb. It took five minutes to get the skill screen to appear, and that's after the character literally got sucked into a normal computer monitor. >_>

reviewed.titleEN: Easygoing Territory Defense by the Optimistic Lord: Production Magic Turns a Nameless Village into the Strongest Fortified City
reviewed.titleJP: お気楽領主の楽しい領地防衛 ～生産系魔術で名もなき村を最強の城塞都市に～
reviewed.review: The story and character designs aren't interesting. But... it has way too much good animation and production for what it's doing. For example: if you watch the first minute of the show, it has a really cool intro sequence—however, it's just used to talk about being reincarnated into another young noble's body, which is a stupid waste of an actually really cool animation sequence. There are other interesting animation and interaction choices and segments, but the whole story feels pretty dumb, not like something I'm gonna watch.

reviewed.titleEN: An Adventurer's Daily Grind at Age 29
reviewed.titleJP: 29歳独身中堅冒険者の日常
reviewed.review: The show is the most definitive 5-out-of-10 that I may have ever seen. It's not terrible; nothing is terrible, nothing is good. Everything is there, boring, and fine... I guess. It's another adventure-dungeon show, and this one's twist is that there's an abandoned little orphan girl—kind of a cute, Anya-Forger-esque thing, but not as well done. There is literally no reason to watch this. There's also no reason to hate it, no reason to like it.

reviewed.titleJP: 魔術師クノンは見えている
reviewed.review: I'm very confused by this show, because it looked like it was trying to be a serious magic show, something about a sorcerer who can't see. But then the intro made it look like it might be almost like a silly school thing, with the character out of place at a school like Mashle. Then there's the main character, who's supposedly been blind forever but has made no adaptations to being blind at all—literally walking around gingerly, being led by his kyonyuu servants. It's very confusing, and I'm not interested enough in it to find out if the confusion will ever be resolved.

reviewed.titleJP: 勇者刑に処す 懲罰勇者9004隊刑務記録
reviewed.review: I wasn't quite sure what to expect. I saw the first episode was an hour long, and I was, based on the title, very sus. But this show has proved to be pretty darn cool-looking. The animation is top-notch, production values across the whole thing are excellent, and the script seems pretty solid. I haven't seen any ridiculous, dumb tropes or anything yet. So I have high hopes for this show.

reviewed.titleJP: 「お前ごときが魔王に勝てると思うな」と勇者パーティを追放されたので、王都で気ままに暮らしたい
reviewed.review: The show isn't great by any stretch of the imagination. But I did put it on, and I sat there through 12 minutes and I didn't end my life. I think the worst part about it is the stupid thing of having stats and screens and such, but I don't see any direct screens for the person. The rest of it seems kind of OK. The animation quality is not great, but I've definitely seen other things where I struggled to even make it through three minutes.

reviewed.titleEN: Noble Reincarnation: Born Blessed, So I'll Obtain Ultimate Power
reviewed.titleJP: 貴族転生 ～恵まれた生まれから最強の力を得る～
reviewed.review: I didn't have high hopes for this, and I have not been defeated. The episode started with a "skip recap" button—that's a good sign, a show starting the very first episode with the ability to skip the recap, and I wish I had a button that said "skip episode" or "skip show." ... Oh dear God, there are still another 30 seconds left, and now we're into the exposition. We get the show's stats screen, but here's the twist: everyone in the show can see everyone else's stats. It's so dumb. The best thing about the show is that in the opening it shows the king's armor and makes him look like the bad guy from Ghosts 'n Goblins.

reviewed.titleEN: You Can't Be In a Rom-Com with Your Childhood Friends!
reviewed.titleJP: 幼馴染とはラブコメにならない
reviewed.review: This one is like a super ecchi version of "To Heart." It's fine for what it is. If you watch the first minute or two of it and it entertains you, then that's the show. I'll give it a point for actually having an opening that they played during the first episode.

reviewed.titleEN: There was a Cute Girl in the Hero's Party, so I Tried Confessing to Her
reviewed.titleJP: 勇者パーティーにかわいい子がいたので、告白してみた。
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: I don't even know what the point of this is. The art is just atrociously bad; they apply all these dumb filters on top of everything, and it's really, really low quality. Why bother? It's not like there's anything super special about this. I ended up watching it for 11 minutes and 18 seconds because I was folding laundry, and I kept wondering if they were gonna get to something that was a hook beyond literally the title of the show. They did not.

reviewed.titleJP: 綺麗にしてもらえますか。
reviewed.review: They made a show about someone running a one-person laundry shop in Atami (which is a little south of Tokyo). It's actually kind of charming and kind of cool, 'cause you get to see some of the more technical details of doing laundry, and I don't hate the first 8 minutes of it.

reviewed.titleEN: The Demon King's Daughter Is Too Kind!!
reviewed.titleJP: 魔王の娘は優しすぎる!!
reviewed.review: I mean, I guess this show is fine? It's nothing special. The title of the show tells you the entire plot. Nothing of note here. Maybe the manga is fine.

reviewed.titleJP: 勇者パーティを追い出された器用貧乏
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: First show of the season, I'm a minute and twenty seconds into it, and I'm already giving this four out of five Kiritos and four out of five Status Screen Overlays. Correction: I'm bumping this up to five out of five for both of those, so it's a perfect show to start this season.
